name: Ratio & proportion
description: Ratio notation and sharing in a ratio, direct and inverse proportion.

questions.prompt: Red and blue counters are in the ratio 4:3. There are 20 red counters. Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: For every 4 red counters there are 3 blue counters

questions.explanation: 20 red means the ratio was scaled up 5 times, so the blue count is 3 × 5 = 15 and the total is 20 + 15 = 35. Taking 1 off 20 to get 19, or adding 4 and 3 to get 19, treats the ratio as a difference. The ratio compares red to blue, so the whole is 7 parts, and blue is 3/7 of the counters, not 3/4.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.
questions.explanation: A ratio is simplified by dividing both parts by the same number: 4:6 and 6:9 divide by 3, and 10:15 divides by 5, all giving 2:3. Taking 1 off each part, as in 4:6 to 3:5, changes the relationship instead of keeping it the same.

questions.prompt: The ratio of red to blue counters in a box is 2:5. What fraction of the counters are red?
questions.explanation: The ratio 2:5 makes 7 parts altogether, 2 of them red, so red is 2/7 of the counters. 2/5 compares red with blue only, which is a part-to-part comparison. 5/7 is the fraction that is blue, and 5/2 puts the parts the wrong way round and is greater than one.

questions.prompt: In a class the ratio of boys to girls is 3:4. Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: The class is divided into 7 equal parts by the ratio
The number of girls is 3/4 of the number of boys

questions.explanation: The ratio 3:4 gives 7 parts in total, so boys are 3/7 of the class and girls are 4/7. Writing 3/4 compares one group with the other rather than with the whole class. Since there are more girls than boys, the number of girls is 4/3 of the number of boys, not 3/4.

questions.prompt: A recipe for 4 people uses 300 g of rice. How much rice is needed for 10 people?
questions.explanation: Find the amount for one person first: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 g, then multiply by 10 to get 750 g. 600 g is only enough for 8 people. 375 g is 5 people's worth. 900 g is three times 300, which serves 12 people.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: If 3 pens cost £1.50, then 6 pens cost £3.00
If 3 pens cost £1.50, then 6 pens cost £4.50
If 5 kg of flour costs £4, then 10 kg costs £8
If 5 kg of flour costs £4, then 15 kg costs £12
If 2 workers build a wall in 6 hours, 4 workers build it in 12 hours
A car going at a steady speed covers 120 miles in 3 hours, having covered 40 miles in 1 hour

questions.explanation: When quantities are in direct proportion, doubling one doubles the other: twice the pens cost twice as much, and three times the flour costs three times as much. Adding £1.50 and £3.00 is not the point — £4.50 would price 9 pens. For workers and time the relationship is the other way round: more workers means less time, so 4 workers take 3 hours, not 12.

questions.prompt: Six workers take 4 days to build a wall. How long would twelve workers take, working at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Twice as many workers do the job in half the time, so 12 workers take 2 days. Doubling the time to 8 days treats this as direct proportion. Leaving it at 4 days ignores the extra workers, and 72 days multiplies the workers by the days instead of dividing.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: If 4 people take 9 hours, then 2 people take 18 hours
If 4 people take 9 hours, then 2 people take 4.5 hours
If 3 taps fill a tank in 20 minutes, then 6 taps fill it in 10 minutes
If 3 taps fill a tank in 20 minutes, then 6 taps fill it in 40 minutes
Doubling the number of machines halves the time taken
More workers always means the job takes longer

questions.explanation: For a fixed job, workers and time are inversely proportional: halving the workers doubles the time (2 people take 18 hours), and doubling the machines halves the time (6 taps take 10 minutes). Treating these as direct proportion gives 4.5 hours and 40 minutes. More workers means less time, provided everyone works at the same rate.

questions.prompt: Sweets are shared between two children in the ratio 3:2. There are 30 sweets. How many does the child with the larger share get?
questions.explanation: The ratio 3:2 has 5 parts, so each part is 30 ÷ 5 = 6 sweets. The larger share is 3 parts, which is 18. 12 is the smaller share, so that swaps the children over. 20 comes from dividing 30 by 3 rather than by 5, and 15 splits the sweets evenly.

Both parts must be in the same unit. 2 hours is 120 minutes, and 40:120 divides by 40 to give 1:3. Dividing 40 by 2 without converting gives 20:1, which compares different units. Reading 40 minutes as 0.4 of the second part, or as one hour, gives 1:2 or 2:1.

questions.prompt: In a bag, 3/5 of the counters are red. The rest are blue. What is the ratio of red to blue counters?
questions.explanation: If 3/5 are red then 2/5 are blue, so red to blue is 3:2. The ratio 3:5 is red to the whole bag, not red to blue. 5:3 puts the whole before the blue part, and 2:3 reverses the order.

questions.prompt: £240 is shared in the ratio 2:3:5. What is the largest share?
questions.explanation: The ratio has 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 parts, so each part is £240 ÷ 10 = £24. The largest share is 5 parts, which is £120. £48 and £72 are the two smaller shares. £100 would come from dividing by 12 instead of 10, which is not the number of parts.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: In the ratio 1:2:3 the largest share is 3/5 of the total
£60 shared in the ratio 1:2:3 gives £10, £20 and £30
£60 shared in the ratio 1:2:3 gives £15, £30 and £45
The ratio 1:2:3 is the same as 2:4:6
The ratio 1:2:3 is the same as 1:2:4

questions.explanation: The parts of 1:2:3 add to 6, so each part of £60 is £10 and the shares are £10, £20 and £30. The largest share is 3 out of 6 parts, which is 1/2 of the total, not 3/5. £15, £30 and £45 would need 8 parts. Multiplying every part by the same number keeps a ratio the same, so 1:2:3 = 2:4:6; changing only the last part does not.

questions.prompt: At a show the ratio of adults to children is 5:3. There are 40 adults. How many children are there?
questions.explanation: 40 adults is 5 parts, so each part is 8 people, and children are 3 parts: 3 × 8 = 24. Stopping at 8 gives only one part. 15 is 5 × 3, which multiplies the two parts of the ratio together. 64 adds the adults to the children's share without working out the parts.

questions.prompt: Paint is mixed from red and white in the ratio 2:5. Tom uses 600 ml of white paint. How much red paint does he need?
questions.explanation: 600 ml is 5 parts, so each part is 120 ml, and red is 2 parts: 2 × 120 = 240 ml. 1200 ml doubles the white instead of finding the red, and 300 ml halves the white rather than using the ratio. 840 ml adds the two figures instead of scaling them.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.
questions.explanation: Divide by the denominator and multiply by the numerator: 1/2 of 40 is 20, 1/4 of 40 is 10, 3/4 of 40 is 30 and 1/5 of 45 is 9. 2/3 of 9 is 6, not 3 — 3 is only one third. 3/5 of 20 is 12, not 15: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 and 4 × 3 = 12.
